sections.hypothesis: Holding BTC or ETH sized by 50% / recent volatility (capped at fully in) gives a better risk-adjusted return than holding fully, after costs. Also an attribution test: trend-vol-target is a trend score times exactly this size, so comparing the two shows which half earns trend-vol-target's result.
sections.rationale: Moreira and Muir (Journal of Finance, 2017) found that scaling exposure down when recent volatility is high improves Sharpe in equities, because volatility rises in crashes faster than expected returns do; a 2025 paper reports the same for crypto momentum ('Cryptocurrency momentum has (not) its moments'). Its out-of-sample record in equities is debated. Weak points: crypto's best days also come in high-volatility spells, so cutting exposure then may cut the rallies too; and a 30-day window reacts after a crash has started. Context: after 139+ trials every bet against the trend has failed, cross-sectional momentum over small coins failed (-92% drawdown), and the one strategy marked Pursue is trend-vol-target on BTC daily (Sharpe 1.21 vs 1.07 for holding on the current config, but +639% vs +1,420% return). This note is one of five momentum ideas tested together on 2026-11-13; five ideas at once are five or more trials, so a single pass is weaker evidence than it looks.
sections.rules: Daily bars. Target weight = min(1, 0.50 / annualised volatility of the last 30 daily log returns); cash until 30 returns exist. Rebalanced daily within the 2% band. Same volatility estimate and target as trend-vol-target's defaults, so the two differ only by the trend votes. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band; long only, spot; 10 bps fee, square-root impact; spread 1 bp for single-coin runs, by the coin's volume band for universe runs. Every strategy starts cold at the first month: cash until its lookbacks fill, the same convention as every earlier test.
sections.falsification: BTCUSDT 1d and ETHUSDT 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10, defaults, 330 USDT, run once each. Reject unless, on both: (1) Sharpe above buy-and-hold's; (2) max drawdown no worse than buy-and-hold's; (3) total return beats the market held at the strategy's average exposure; (4) break-even cost at least twice the cost paid. Attribution, decided now: compared with trend-vol-target on the current config (runs 20261113-073755-da13da BTC, Sharpe 1.21, and 20261113-073757-155a79 ETH, Sharpe 1.23), a Sharpe within 0.10 of trend-vol-target's means the trend votes add little and vol-hold is the simpler explanation; lower by more than 0.10 means the trend votes do the work.
sections.parameters: vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50. Only these are pre-registered.
sections.costs: Daily resizing as volatility moves, limited by the 2% band: perhaps 5-10x turnover a year at about 11 bps a side.
